evidenceAudit.scope: Pregnant and postpartum women (up to 42 days after birth or abortion) with suspected infection and organ dysfunction in India: recognition, the first-hour bundle, empiric antibiotics by source, fluids, vasopressors and source control. Antibiotics follow the NCDC-ICMR National Treatment Guidelines (NTG) 2025 sections on puerperal sepsis, chorioamnionitis and septic abortion; resuscitation targets follow the Society for Maternal-Fetal Medicine (SMFM) Consult #67 (2023).
findings: Puerperal sepsis definition and diagnostic features, piperacillin-tazobactam first line, clindamycin with gentamicin in penicillin allergy, carbapenem for septic shock, and MRSA cover with vancomycin or teicoplanin checked against NCDC-ICMR NTG 2025 section 6.8.
Chorioamnionitis regimens (ampicillin, gentamicin and metronidazole; piperacillin-tazobactam when septic) checked against NTG section 6.10; septic abortion against NTG section 6.3.

Antibiotics within 1 hour, lactate and cultures, 1–2 L balanced crystalloid in the first 3 hours, norepinephrine to a mean arterial pressure of 65 mmHg, hydrocortisone 50 mg every 6 hours for refractory shock, thromboprophylaxis and source control checked against SMFM Consult #67, recommendations and Figure 2.
NTG and SMFM differ on first-line antibiotics for endometritis; shown side by side.
unverifiedSections: No Indian national maternal sepsis bundle could be opened; resuscitation steps are from SMFM Consult #67.
Norepinephrine is given as a titrated infusion; starting rates are not stated in SMFM and follow the intensive care unit (ICU) protocol.
Thromboprophylaxis drug and dose are not specified in SMFM; follow the obstetric thromboprophylaxis protocol.
Antenatal corticosteroids for fetal lung maturity are mentioned by SMFM without a dose here; use the preterm birth protocol.
Paediatric doses do not apply; adolescents in pregnancy receive adult doses.
Drug cautions and contraindications without a source tag are general pharmacology statements and need formulary confirmation.
US labels (DailyMed) were used where Indian sources give no dose; confirm against the Indian product label (CDSCO) and hospital formulary.

pathophysiology.summary: Maternal sepsis is life-threatening organ dysfunction caused by infection during pregnancy, childbirth, after abortion or in the postpartum period. Common sources are the genital tract (endometritis, chorioamnionitis, septic abortion), urinary tract, lungs, breast and wounds. Normal pregnancy changes mask early signs, so deterioration can be sudden. Treat as an emergency: antibiotics within an hour, fluids, vasopressors if needed, and early source control (SMFM 2023; NTG 2025).
keyMechanisms: Organisms ascend from the vagina into the uterus after delivery, procedures or retained tissue.
A dysregulated host response causes vasodilatation, capillary leak and organ hypoperfusion; lactate rises.
Pregnancy lowers colloid oncotic pressure, so aggressive fluids cause pulmonary oedema more easily (SMFM p. B10).
Group A streptococcus and clostridia can cause rapid toxic shock and necrotising infection (NTG section 6.8).

symptoms: Fever or chills; feeling very unwell
Foul-smelling or purulent vaginal discharge (NTG section 6.8)
physicalSigns: Uterus involuting less than 2 cm/day in the first 8 days (NTG section 6.8)
Uterine or wound tenderness; breast redness; chest signs
redFlags: Mean arterial pressure under 65 mmHg or lactate over 2 mmol/L after fluids: septic shock (SMFM p. B3)
Altered mental state, low urine output, low platelets
Rapid spreading skin changes or severe pain out of proportion: necrotising infection (SMFM Table 4)
Fetal tachycardia or distress in antenatal sepsis
precipitants: Prolonged rupture of membranes and prolonged labour
Caesarean birth, retained placenta or products

differentials.distinguishingFeatures: Sudden breathlessness, pleuritic pain, often without fever; computed tomography (CT) pulmonary angiogram.
Shock with visible or concealed bleeding, no fever.
Hypertension, proteinuria, low platelets and raised liver enzymes without infection.
Sudden collapse and coagulopathy around delivery.

diagnosticCriteria.threshold: Serious genital tract infection within 42 days of delivery; 2 or more of pelvic pain, oral temperature 38.5°C or more, abnormal discharge, delayed uterine involution (under 2 cm/day in first 8 days).
Infection with organ dysfunction, scored by the Sequential Organ Failure Assessment (SOFA) with pregnancy-adjusted interpretation.
Vasopressors needed to keep mean arterial pressure 65 mmHg and lactate over 2 mmol/L despite adequate fluids.

ruleIn.clinicalRationale: Take before antibiotics without delaying them beyond 1 hour (SMFM Figure 2).

clinicalManagement.title: First-hour bundle
actions: Cultures and lactate, then broad-spectrum intravenous antibiotics (SMFM rec 8; Figure 2).
Start 1–2 L balanced crystalloid over the first 3 hours; reassess often (SMFM rec 10–11).
Treat as an emergency: senior obstetric, anaesthetic and critical care review (SMFM rec 2).

clinicalManagement.title: Septic shock
actions: Norepinephrine to keep mean arterial pressure at 65 mmHg if hypotension persists (SMFM rec 14; Figure 2).
Hydrocortisone if no response to norepinephrine or epinephrine 0.25 micrograms/kg/min or more for at least 4 hours (SMFM Figure 2).
Transfer to intensive care unit (ICU) or high-dependency care.

clinicalManagement.title: Source control
clinicalManagement.timeframe: As soon as a source is found
actions: Evacuate retained products, drain abscesses, deliver if intra-amniotic infection, regardless of gestational age when the uterus is the source (SMFM rec 9, 18).
Necrotising infection or myometrial necrosis: debridement and hysterectomy (SMFM p. B9).

clinicalManagement.title: Ongoing care
actions: De-escalate antibiotics with culture results; daily review (SMFM p. B9).
Pharmacological thromboprophylaxis in septic shock (SMFM rec 16); insulin if glucose over 180 mg/dL (SMFM rec 17); early enteral feeding (SMFM Figure 2).
Breastfeeding usually continues; check drug compatibility.

medicationPlan.note: Antibiotic choices and doses from NCDC-ICMR NTG 2025 (sections 6.3, 6.8, 6.10); give within 1 hour. Resuscitation (crystalloid 1–2 L, norepinephrine to mean arterial pressure 65 mmHg, hydrocortisone 200 mg/day for refractory shock) from SMFM Consult #67. Source control is essential. Not clinically reviewed.

teaching.scope: Sepsis in pregnancy and after birth or abortion.
learningObjectives: Recognise maternal sepsis despite pregnancy physiology.
Choose antibiotics by source and achieve source control.
keyPoints: Fluids 1–2 L balanced crystalloid in 3 hours; watch for pulmonary oedema.
Norepinephrine to mean arterial pressure 65 mmHg.
Find and remove the source: retained products, abscess, infected uterus.
pitfalls: Attributing tachycardia to pain or labour.
Missing group A streptococcal toxic shock.
